title: The parity of the rounded-up half is decided by m mod 4
statement: For every natural m, the parity of m - div m 2 (that is, of the rounded-up half of m) is decided by m modulo 4: it is EVEN when m is 4q or 4q+3, and ODD when m is 4q+1 or 4q+2, where q := div (div m 2) 2. The residue class is stated structurally as an equation on m rather than through a `mod 4` term, because `Nat.div`/`Nat.mod` are stuck at a symbolic argument; the four shapes named are exhaustive and pairwise distinct, so the disjunction determines the parity in both directions. Parity is `Nat.Even`/`Nat.Odd`, this kernel's existential predicates. `Kernel::axiom_footprint` for this declaration is EMPTY. WHY IT MATTERS. At p := 2m+1 the four shapes are p = 8q+1, 8q+3, 8q+5, 8q+7, so this is exactly the p mod 8 classification the SECOND SUPPLEMENTARY LAW of quadratic reciprocity needs: Gauss's lemma reduces 2^m mod p to (-1)^(m - div m 2), and this theorem decides that sign (F:int-secondsupplementarylaw).

provenance.source: Derived mechanically from the unfiltered emit of `cargo run -q --release -p axeyum-lean-kernel --example kernel_declaration_projection`, which prints one TSV row per declaration whose fields are (prelude, kind, display name, axiom-footprint size, direct type declarations, direct declarations, direct theorems, Kernel::render_lean(declaration.ty())). formal.statement is that last field verbatim; depends_on is the direct-theorem column intersected with this ledger's registered facts; axiom_footprint is the footprint-size column, cross-checked by the whole-prelude nat_axiom_inventory run recorded in the second evidence row. No field was hand-transcribed and no prose was authored. `title`, `statement` and `notes` were then REPLACED by hand (lane second-supplementary-law, ADR-1150); every other field is the generator's output unmodified.

notes: Route (`nat_prelude/half_ceil_parity.rs`): `Nat.even_or_odd` applied twice, at m and then at the computed half h := div m 2, with q := div h 2. That PRODUCES the four classes -- m = h+h or succ (h+h), each with h = q+q or succ (q+q) -- so no division ever has to reduce, which is the point: a mod-4 hypothesis could not have been evaluated at a symbolic m. Both count evaluations are one application of `Nat.add_sub_cancel_left` (sub (add x y) x = y). Even m: at (h, h), giving sub (add h h) h = h. Odd m: at (h, succ h), whose statement is sub (add h (succ h)) h = succ h -- and add h (succ h) is DEFINITIONALLY succ (add h h), because Nat.add recurses on its right argument and the literal succ there reduces with no succ_add rewrite. That is why the symbolic side is kept on the left throughout the file. The m = 4q+3 case is the only one needing a real lemma: succ (succ (q+q)) is add (succ q) (succ q) only up to `nat_prelude/parity.rs`'s `succ_double_eq`, which was already there (private) and was exposed rather than rebuilt. The classification table was re-derived in Python before any Rust was written, not inherited from a plan: python3 -c "import collections; agg=collections.defaultdict(set); [agg[m%4].add(((2*m+1)%8, (m-(m//2))%2)) for m in range(200)]; print([(k, sorted(agg[k])) for k in sorted(agg)])" gives 0->(1,even), 1->(3,odd), 2->(5,odd), 3->(7,even).
